headline: Graph and network models link metabolite structures, microbes, and protein interactions
label: Network Guided Deep Learning
summary: Recent preprints apply network-based deep learning to metabolite annotation, biomarker nomination, and interaction prediction.
synthesis: The common thread is conditioning learned models on biological network structure, whether protein networks, microbial association networks, molecular neighborhoods, or knowledge graphs. A CNN over a protein network nominates COPD-comorbidity biomarker candidates, which are tested on public transcriptomic data. A graph neural network applied to individual microbial association networks from HMP2/iHMP metagenomes identifies a co-abundant Bacteroidales module driving IBD prediction, with interpretation of learned patterns as a central output. In metabolomics, DEEPNET-LLM restricts de novo structure prediction from MS/MS spectra to molecular-community neighborhoods, and FeatureMAP applies network guidance to LC-MS annotation and module discovery. A random forest using MINT embeddings predicts differential protein-protein interactions across cell conditions. What is new across these items is the explicit use of network neighborhoods as the constraint on prediction, annotation, or interpretation.
